sections.h2: Which way of selling fits a Troy house?
sections.html:
Troy owners can go through an agent, handle the sale alone, or take an all-cash bid. Every version finishes with a deed, a state transfer tax return and a filing at the Rensselaer County Clerk, so the choice turns on speed, condition and how much effort you can give it.

A listing pays off for a house that is ready to move into, because mortgage buyers order an appraisal and an inspection. Direct cash deals turn up more often where repairs were put off, a tenant is in the way, a code question is open or an estate is involved. In all cases, set aside your latest tax bill, any lease and repair receipts.

  • Agent route: the biggest audience, along with prep work, showings and a bank-driven closing.
  • Solo route: no commission, but all contracts and haggling are yours.
  • All-cash route: the house sells as it stands and the closing date is negotiable.

Judge each bid by the cash you would leave with after tax balances, liens and the transfer tax, rather than the number on page one.

sections.h2: Troy as a place to sell
sections.html:
Troy is the Rensselaer County seat, set on the Hudson's east bank just northeast of Albany. It has 50,912 people, a 0.7 percent dip from 2020, on 10.36 square miles of land. Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, Emma Willard School, Russell Sage College and Hudson Valley Community College are all within the city limits.

Ground is flat beside the river and rises sharply eastward to about 500 feet. The north end used to be the separate city of Lansingburgh, and the Poesten Kill and Wynants Kill cut through town on their way to the Hudson. On a sloped lot, buyers may ask how water drains away from the house, so have any answers ready.

US 4 follows River Street, NY 7 uses Hoosick Street, NY 2 runs along Congress Street, and Interstate 787 ends in the city. The Troy and Lansingburgh school districts both serve parts of town, and whichever covers your street sends your school tax bill.

Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $206,500, and just 37.4 percent of homes are occupied by owners. Rents have a median of $1,175 among 21,265 households (2020 to 2024 figures).

With renters in the majority, small landlords and investors shape demand. Selling a two or three-unit building means supplying rent rolls, leases and utility costs. Median household income is $58,477, so price against close comparables instead of a citywide figure.

Troy is humid continental, averaging 25.5 degrees in January with about 42 inches of precipitation yearly, so have the ages of the roof and heating system on hand.

The city assessor builds a roll of about 13,400 properties every year, and 2013 was the last revaluation. A roll that old can sit well away from current prices, so an assessed value is a weak guide to what your house will bring.

Assessment and billing calendar
DateWhat happens
March 1Status date, and the last day to file exemptions
May 1Tentative roll filed; change notices go out that week
Fourth Tuesday of MayGrievance Day hearings
July 1Final roll filed; school, city and county taxes follow it
January and JulyCity and county installments

The Troy and Lansingburgh districts bill school taxes on their own, and penalties on those build monthly after the due date. The Treasurer's Office, 518-279-7115, can give a balance. Owners get a copy of a bill at no cost, while anyone else pays $5.

The Assessor's Office will also estimate taxes without exemptions for a prospective buyer, so a seller can steer a shopper there.

Renewal packets for the senior and disability exemptions go out by mail each fall and are due back before March 1. The city and county income cap is $48,399 of 2025 household income.

  • STAR: first-time applicants go to the NYS Tax Department, not City Hall.
  • Seniors and owners with disabilities: send the signed renewal with your 2025 federal return, or the income worksheet if you do not file.
  • Military service: forms RP-458-a (alternative) and RP-458-b (Cold War).
  • Buyers of newly built homes, owners making capital improvements and owners rehabilitating historic buildings each have their own forms.

Exemptions stay with the owner who qualifies. A buyer files fresh paperwork, which is one reason a bill can climb after a sale. If your senior exemption lowers your bill, warn the buyer's side that their figure will differ.

The Bureau of Code Enforcement handles building permits, housing and construction inspections, vacant building inspections, and certificates of occupancy and compliance. Troy enacted a new zoning ordinance and use maps in April 2023, so check them before you advertise a house as a legal two-family or mixed-use property.

Phone the bureau at 518-279-7180 before listing and ask whether open violations, vacant building requirements or certificate questions are tied to your address. Defects alone rarely stop a direct buyer, though unresolved city paperwork can hold up a closing. If the building has been empty, ask about its vacant building inspection requirements before you sign anything.

sections.h2: Finding out exactly what is owed
sections.html:
Start with the city's searchable tax roll, a document you can scan with your browser's find function by last name, account number or tax map ID. If you do not have the tax map ID, the Rensselaer County property search site shows it. Online payments carry a processing fee, but that fee goes to the outside vendor and not to the city.

Troy issues garbage bills as well as tax bills. Receipts for tax and garbage bills are only handed out when the entire bill is presented with the payment, and the top portion is then stamped as paid and returned. Keep that stamped stub with your closing papers as proof the bill was settled.

City and county installments fall in January and July, and school taxes follow a separate calendar. Ask the Treasurer's Office what is open on each before you agree to a closing date.

sections.h2: Preparing a Troy house for buyers
sections.html:
Before you list or accept a bid, collect the paper a buyer will ask for: your latest tax bill with its stamped stub, any lease and rent ledger, and the receipts for roof, heating and electrical work. Call the Treasurer's Office for a balance and the Bureau of Code Enforcement for open items.

If you live in a rental building, tell tenants early. If the house is vacant, confirm the vacant building rules. A tidy file lets a buyer price the property fast, and it shortens the wait between a handshake and a closing.

faqs.a: The fourth Tuesday of May, which falls on May 25 in 2027. By then the tentative roll has been on file since May 1.

faqs.q: How are city and county taxes paid?
faqs.a: In two installments, one due in January and one in July. School taxes come separately from the Troy or Lansingburgh district, and the Treasurer's Office handles questions about your bill.

faqs.q: What does the state transfer tax cost on a sale?
faqs.a: New York's base tax is $2 per $500 of price and falls on the seller. The return goes to the county clerk with the deed.

faqs.q: Does a senior exemption pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. It belongs to the qualifying owner, so a buyer applies on their own by the March 1 deadline.

faqs.q: Can a Troy house with violations be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Start by asking the Bureau of Code Enforcement what is open at your address, since a direct buyer can accept rough condition but open city items still need attention.
